summary: Abdominal pain is a significant clinical feature in various conditions. In TRAPS, it is the most prominent finding, particularly in childhood [S5|PMC8293050|1409]. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) can also present with abdominal pain, as seen in cases involving a 76-year-old male and a 64-year-old male [S4|PMC9355740|198][S6|PMC9355740|230]. Histopathological features of vitamin E deficiency include steatitis and muscle degeneration, with widespread adipocyte necrosis [S2|PMC7149534|9]. In TRAPS, histopathology reveals a lymphocytic infiltrate with venule cuffing [S5|PMC8293050|1409]. Management of AIHA varies, with treatments including prednisolone and supportive RBC transfusions [S4|PMC9355740|198][S5|PMC9355740|229]. Risk factors such as inflammatory bowel disease and eosinophilic gastroenteritis are noted in specific populations [S3|PMC7149534|34].

map_chunks.summary_text: The literature discusses various conditions affecting mustelids and humans, including vitamin E deficiency leading to steatitis and muscle degeneration [S2|PMC7149534|9]. Inflammatory bowel disease is common in middle-aged and older ferrets [S3|PMC7149534|34]. Several cases of autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) are presented, with symptoms including abdominal pain and fatigue, and treatments involving prednisolone [S4|PMC9355740|198][S5|PMC9355740|229][S6|PMC9355740|230]. Staging criteria for Wilms Tumor (WT) and pediatric renal tumors are also outlined, emphasizing the importance of margin status and lymph node involvement [S7|PMC12232243|621][S8|PMC12232243|643][S9|PMC12232243|648].

map_chunks.summary_text: Residual non-haematogenous tumour can be present after surgery, classified as SIOP local stage III [S1|PMC12232243|690]. Viable or non-viable tumours may involve abdominal-pelvic lymph nodes [S2|PMC12232243|691], and tumour implants may be found anywhere in the abdomen [S3|PMC12232243|697]. Laboratory tests show leukocytosis at 13.1 G/L and eosinophils at 0.55 G/L [S4|PMC9326618|924]. Bacterial smear and viral PCRs were negative [S4|PMC9326618|924]. Skin biopsy indicated inflammatory changes [S4|PMC9326618|924], and direct immunofluorescence revealed C3 deposits [S4|PMC9326618|924]. In TRAPS, abdominal pain is a prominent finding, especially in childhood [S5|PMC8293050|1409]. Histopathology in TRAPS shows lymphocytic infiltrate [S5|PMC8293050|1409]. A 64-year-old male presented with rashes and systemic symptoms [S6|PMC4965535|1431], with a notable 5-cm mass in the axilla and rash extending to the abdomen [S7|PMC4965535|1432].
